Hi Samuel / Elena,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really useful to understand Acme's reliability concerns and the internal SLAs you need to hold for your product. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get a short, focused test scheduled: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary objective: verify provider behavior under sustained load, burst traffic, and simulated region degradation (failover behavior + end-to-end latency impact).
- Key SLOs you care about: availability (target 99.99% for inference), tail latency (p99 < 300ms for small prompts), predictable rate-limiting semantics and transparent error budgets.

Redwood quick differentiators we called out
- Dedicated pools + graceful fallback: customers can reserve capacity and we automatically route to compatible model variants during constrained states.
- Error budget visibility: token-level tracing + alerts and explicit per-route error budgets (not just opaque 429s).
- Intelligent batching + KV caching reduces burst impact while keeping p99 stable.

Suggested next tests (short list)
1) Sustained throughput: 1M tokens/hour for 24 hours to look for drift/queueing effects.
2) Burst + throttling: repeated 30s bursts at 5x steady QPS to observe throttling behavior and 429 vs 503 surface.
3) Failover simulation: single-region outage (route to fallback variant/region) and measure recovery time and dropped requests.
4) Error budget consumption: run a synthetic test to show how error budget is reported and how alerts trigger.

What we need from Acme
- A small set of representative prompts + success criteria (latency / failed request tolerances).
- A contact on your infra team for scheduling the test window and SCIM/API key access.

Attachments: I've attached a short SLO comparison table and our proposed test plan. Ben and Rishi are looped for technical coordination.

Proposed timeline
- Share prompts and contacts by EOD Friday 3/20
- Schedule 2-hour test window next Wed 3/25 (we can adjust)

If that sounds good, we'll provision a dedicated test token and a temporary test cluster (no production traffic).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Samuel — quick technical answers and what we'll deliver before the test window: 

1) Test harness: we provide both options — a lightweight open-source runner (link below) you can run from your infra, or we can run the harness from our side against the dedicated test cluster. For initial validation we recommend you run it to capture end-to-end networking behavior. Link: https://redwood.internal/test-harness/ACME (credentials will be in the test token).

2) Rate limits behavior:
- Soft throttling: for customers on hosted plans we do gradual queueing and shed load; clients will see increased latency and, at sustained overload, 429s.
- Hard limits / Dedicated pools: for dedicated capacity, we enforce per-seat concurrency limits and return polite 503/429 with consistent retry-after headers when capacity is temporarily exhausted. In practice, Redwood aims to avoid hard throttling during a short burst by using short-term autoscale and batching; only under sustained saturation will we return 429s.
- Recommended client behavior: exponential backoff with jitter starting at 200ms, max 3 retries for user-facing requests; background jobs can retry more aggressively.

3) Isolation: for the test we'll provision a dedicated GPU pool for the window and disable autoscaling to ensure stable capacity during measurements. That gives you a clean baseline vs noisy neighbor effects.

4) Error budgets & observability: we'll provide a read-only dashboard for the test that shows per-route error budget consumption, token-level failure traces, and p50/p95/p99 latency breakdowns. We'll also stream the raw telemetry if you need to ingest it into your monitoring (Prometheus/Grafana).

Action items I'll take:
- Provision test cluster + token and share credentials by EOD Friday 3/20.
- Upload the sample load scripts and a brief runbook (redwood-test-harness-instructions.txt).
- Coordinate with Rishi for on-call support during the test window.

Thanks,
Ben
